routes.label: Compare areas using a shared side

question:
Rectangle \(ABCD,\) pictured below, shares \(50\%\) of its area with square \(EFGH.\) Square \(EFGH\) shares \(20\%\) of its area with rectangle \(ABCD.\) What is \(\dfrac{AB}{AD}?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2010_AMC_12A_Q03_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The overlap has the full width of the square and the full height of rectangle \(ABCD\). This lets us turn the area percentages into length relationships: when two rectangles have the same width, their areas have the same ratio as their heights, because area equals width times height.

Let \(h=AD>0\), and let \(s>0\) be the square's side length. The overlap and the square both have width \(s\). Since the overlap is \(20\%=\frac15\) of the square's area, its height \(h\) is one fifth of \(s\). Thus the square's side contains five such heights:
\[
s=5h.
\]
The overlap and rectangle \(ABCD\) both have height \(h\), so their areas have the same ratio as their widths. The overlap is \(50\%=\frac12\) of the rectangle's area, making its width \(s\) half of \(AB\). Therefore
\[
AB=2s=10h.
\]
Since \(h>0\),
\[
\frac{AB}{AD}=\frac{10h}{h}=\boxed{10}.
\]
The answer is choice E.
